themes_detail.label: Park Noise Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints in parks spiked to 16 complaints last week vs. 0.6 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 2460% increase (z-score: 11.67)—suggesting a sudden, severe disruption to outdoor recreational spaces this week that warrants immediate investigation.
evidence: 16 park noise complaints last week vs. 0.6 weekly baseline (2460% spike)
Z-score of 11.67 indicates statistically extreme deviation from 8-week pattern
Spike appeared suddenly with no gradual escalation pattern
reporting_angles: What triggered the sudden influx of park noise complaints? (new event, construction, congregation, or seasonal factor?)
Which parks are affected and what times of day are residents complaining?

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Deterioration Spike
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints jumped to 18 THIS WEEK vs. 6.4 weekly average—a 182% increase (z-score: 3.93)—indicating rapid deterioration of pedestrian infrastructure in the district.
evidence: 18 sidewalk condition complaints this week vs. 6.4 weekly average over 8 weeks (182% increase)
Z-score of 3.93 indicates statistically significant deviation
Aligns with long-standing CB budget requests for street/infrastructure upgrades
reporting_angles: Which corridors or neighborhoods in Hillcrest/Fresh Meadows show the worst sidewalk damage?
Is this weather-related (freeze-thaw cycle) or infrastructure neglect that requires capital investment?

themes_detail.label: Animal Infestation Concerns
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary animal/private property complaints surged to 3 last week vs. 0.4 weekly average—a 700% spike (z-score: 3.77)—suggesting a potential pest or wildlife infestation problem emerging in the district.
evidence: 3 complaints last week vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (700% increase)
Z-score of 3.77 indicates statistically significant anomaly
No prior pattern of animal-related complaints in district
reporting_angles: What types of animals are residents reporting and in which neighborhoods?
Is this linked to sanitation issues, construction activity, or seasonal migration?

themes_detail.label: Curb Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints reached 22 three weeks ago vs. 6.8 weekly average—a 226% increase (z-score: 2.86)—indicating sustained damage to street infrastructure that may require capital repair work.
evidence: 22 curb condition complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 6.8 weekly average (226% increase)
Z-score of 2.86 indicates statistically significant spike
Part of broader pattern of street/infrastructure complaints alongside sidewalk issues
reporting_angles: How extensive is curb damage across the district and what's causing accelerated deterioration?
Should this be bundled with sidewalk repair into a broader infrastructure capital request?

themes_detail.label: Heat/Hot Water Baseline High
themes_detail.summary: Heat and hot water complaints remain the 5th-highest complaint category at 1,227 over 90 days with no current spike, but persistent high volume suggests chronic housing infrastructure problems that the CB has repeatedly requested building inspector resources to address.
evidence: 1,227 heat/hot water complaints over 90 days (4th highest by volume)
Community board has repeated requests for additional building inspectors (year-over-year budget request)
Suggests systemic code enforcement and landlord compliance issues
reporting_angles: Which buildings are repeat offenders for heat/hot water violations and why aren't penalties forcing compliance?
How would additional building inspectors improve enforcement in the district?
